mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 6 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 6 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 7.0% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 7.0% in a month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in consumer credit (RSAFS) and a reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a coordinated monetary and credit policy easing that boosts aggregate demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where both RSAFS declines and FEDFUNDS falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In regimes of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 99.0), supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output signal an impending economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO < 99.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 6 months indicates strong consumer confidence and residential investment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where HOUST has increased over the prior 6 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.5% in a single month, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where both PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In regimes of high unemployment (UNRATE > 7.0%), the labor market is weak, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where UNRATE > 7.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
